name: Crystal Venture Partners
identity_check: Confirmed as Crystal Venture Partners (crystalventurepartners.com), the New York early-stage firm led by Jonathan H. F. Crystal. He was CFO of his family's insurance brokerage, Crystal & Company, until its 2018 sale to Alliant. The firm invests at pre-seed and seed at the intersection of insurance, risk and technology. Its site reposts Fortune's 2025-10-06 article on the $33M first fund, which matches the Shai Goldman fund-list lead (spelled 'Crystal Ventture Partners' there). TechCrunch and Pulse 2.0 use the same name and cite Jonathan Crystal as managing partner. The Advance release calls it 'Crystal Ventures', with Jonathan Crystal as Managing Partner, so that is the same firm. Ruled out as different investors: Crystal Ventures and Crystal Venture Funds (separate investor profiles in search results), Crystal Internet Ventures (CB Insights) and Crystal Tech Fund (a 2014 Washington, D.C. fund in the Goldman list).

thesis_text.value: Sector-specific early-stage fund for insurance, risk and technology, backing businesses where handling risk is what customers pay for. It expects AI to let specialist underwriters and brokers build sizeable companies on insurers' capital, and new warranties and coverage to grow around AI adoption. It offers two decades of insurance-operator relationships to help founders win capacity and credit.

open_items: No application form or apply URL. The homepage Contact link and the end of the 2026 essay point to a 'deals@' mailbox (not recorded), so cold inbound is inferred as yes from that published deal-flow address.
Nothing found on investing in Indian founders or requiring a US entity. The portfolio is mostly US; Novella has a Tel Aviv R&D centre, and MIC Global is a pre-fund investment.

No street address on the site. HQ comes from 'New York-based' in Fortune and the firm's own essay. SEC EDGAR Form D was not checked, so the Fund I legal name and final-close date are not confirmed. The 2025-10-06 close date is Fortune's publication date ('just closed').
LPs are not named beyond 'family offices and global insurance companies' (Fortune). No Fund II found; Fortune says he is 'not actively raising his next fund'.

No page found naming Crystal in a round for these Fund I companies on the homepage: Nevado (nevado.ai), Sheltra (getsheltra.com), Kinro (kinro.ai, which search results describe as YC Spring 2026) and an unnamed company 'strengthening the nation's construction backbone through AI-powered, integrated manufacturing'. That last one is the only industrial-adjacent name in the portfolio.

Sixfold's $30M Series B (Coverager, 2026-01-31, led by Brewer Lane) names Bessemer and Salesforce Ventures but not Crystal, so it is not recorded. The six pre-fund investments (NowCerts, MIC Global, Functional FI, Delos, Comulate, CompScience) were made before Fund I. No round pages naming Crystal were checked for them; Jonathan Crystal may have invested personally.
The firm's content page reposts the Travelers-Corvus acquisition release (2024-01-02), which does not mention Crystal. Its Corvus link is not established and is not recorded.

Crystal led only Charter Space among the rounds found; it participated in all others. Fortune says Crystal invested in Bright Harbor and Sixfold before their seed and Series A respectively, but the earlier Bright Harbor round was not found.

Gyde: the Business Wire release reposted on the firm's site shows no dateline date. The firm's page is dated Jan 28, 2026, but the firm's dates proved unreliable (Sixfold), so the date is recorded to the month. Bright Harbor HQ and founding years are not stated for several companies (Sixfold, Advance, Gyde, WithCoverage, Bright Harbor).
The NY Venture Summit 2026 attendee-list lead was not verified on a fetched page.

Other team-page members not recorded as partners: Cat Jordan (Chief of Staff) and Isabel Fields (Associate). Partner focus_sectors are set to fintech (insurance) because the firm covers insurance only.
